place: the Juicero Press laid out part by part
a tray of chopped fruit and vegetables

moments.what: the Juicero logo sticker drops in

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Juicero sold a $699 juicer that only pressed its own packs.

place: a chopping board of cut vegetables

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Each pack held chopped fruit and vegetables, sold for $5 to $7, one glass at a time. So why buy the machine?

place: Kleiner Perkins' sign in Menlo Park

moments.what: a print of Sand Hill Road lands on the pile
the Kleiner Perkins print lands, a lower third

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It launched in San Francisco, backed by Google's venture arm and Kleiner Perkins.

place: a kitchen counter where the press sat

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In January, Juicero cut the press from $699 to $399.

place: a kitchen counter where hands squeeze fruit

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then in April, Bloomberg reporters skipped the press and squeezed the packs with their bare hands.

place: a hand squeezing a lemon over a blender cup

moments.what: a label: nearly the same juice

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Their hands got nearly as much juice out, and faster. So who still needed the machine?

place: a shop door with a closed sign

moments.what: cut to an empty office, a stamp: SHUT DOWN

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That September, Juicero shut down for good.

place: the poster over a glass of fresh juice

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: By then, investors had put about $120M into a juicer that two bare hands could match.

place: a lemon press over a sink
the Juicero Press from the first frame

moments.what: push in on the lemon press
back to the Juicero Press from the first frame

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The machine or the packs: which one sank Juicero? Next time you squeeze a lemon, remember,
